title: Finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$.
For an object $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology sheaves of the
finite-torsion constructibility condition
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], say that $K$ has *finite Tor
amplitude* if it has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] for some integers $a\leq b$, that is, for every sheaf $M$ of
$A$-modules placed in degree zero, the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] of the derived tensor product [def-weil-derived-tensor] satisfy

$$
 \mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_A M)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b].
$$

Define $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ as the full subcategory of $D^b_c(Y,A)$ of such objects; it is a full triangulated subcategory [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ by [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated].
For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, a derived-complete bounded constructible
complex [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], say that $K$ has
finite Tor amplitude if there are integers $a\leq b$ such that every derived reduction $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction],
$j\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, one interval
independent of $j$, and define $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ as the full subcategory of the triangulated category $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] of such objects; it is a full triangulated subcategory by [lem-weil-integral-ctf-triangulated]. At
field coefficients the finite-Tor subcategories are, by definition, the
bounded constructible rationalized category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and its common-stage algebraically closed
coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]:

$$
 D^b_{ctf}(Y,E):=D^b_c(Y,E),
 \qquad
 D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Qlb):=D^b_c(Y,\Qlb).
$$

The second equality is interpreted in the finite-stage triangulated
2-colimit. For $A_{E,n}$, finite Tor amplitude is an additional condition and
does not follow from bounded constructibility. At the integral stage it is
imposed by the displayed definition; a separate residue-field argument, which is a statement and not part of this definition,
proves that every object of the derived-complete constructible category
in fact satisfies it. This conclusion uses the compatibility of all
reductions of one integral object.

Mathlib has no Tor amplitude and no derived tensor product of sheaves of modules (Tor only for abelian monoidal categories with projective resolutions; Module.Flat for modules over rings).

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with uniformizer $\pi_E$, an
integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is
invertible. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$, let
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, regarded as a condensed ring with
coefficient sheaf $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$, and use the derived cohomology
sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and the derived tensor product
over $\Lambda_Y$ ([det-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; [def-weil-derived-tensor]
for finite $\Lambda$). For integers $a\leq b$, an object
$K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has *Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$* if, for
every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda_Y$-modules placed in degree zero,

$$
 \mathcal H^r(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_Y} M)=0
 \qquad\text{for every }r\in\mathbf Z\setminus[a,b],
$$

and it has *finite Tor amplitude* if it has Tor amplitude in some $[a,b]$.
These two conditions make sense, with the same wording, for any commutative
condensed ring $\Lambda$ and any scheme $Y$. Define $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ as
the full subcategory of the bounded constructible category
$D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ [det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] (for
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$: complexes that are bounded with constructible cohomology
sheaves [def-sfb-bounded-constructible-complexes], with the finite-torsion
constructibility condition [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]) on the
objects of finite Tor amplitude. The definition is the same for every
$\Lambda$.

**Well-definedness.** Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ is invariant under
isomorphism, and it widens: Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ implies Tor amplitude in
$[a',b']$ whenever $a'\le a$ and $b\le b'$. If $K$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$ then $K[1]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b-1]$. If
$K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ is a distinguished triangle and $K',K''$ have Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$, so does $K$; and a direct summand of a complex with Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Hence the complexes of
finite Tor amplitude form a thick subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,
and $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ is the intersection of this thick subcategory with
$D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$; it is a full triangulated subcategory.

For $A_{E,n}$, finite Tor amplitude is an additional condition and does not
follow from bounded constructibility. For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ it is automatic,
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)=D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$; this is proved later, see
[lem-integral-ctf-equals-bc].

proof.text:
Invariance under isomorphism is clear, since isomorphic complexes have
isomorphic derived tensor products and cohomology sheaves; widening the
interval is immediate from the definition.

Shift: $K[1]\otimes^{L}M=(K\otimes^{L}M)[1]$, so its cohomology in degree $r$
is that of $K\otimes^{L}M$ in degree $r+1$.

Extensions: $-\otimes^{L}M$ is a triangulated functor, so it turns the
triangle into a distinguished triangle
$K'\otimes^{L}M\to K\otimes^{L}M\to K''\otimes^{L}M\to$, and the long exact
cohomology sequence [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] shows that
$\mathcal H^r(K\otimes^{L}M)$ sits between $\mathcal H^r(K'\otimes^{L}M)$ and
$\mathcal H^r(K''\otimes^{L}M)$, which vanish for $r\notin[a,b]$.

Taking unions over $[a,b]$ (and widening the intervals of the two outer terms
of a triangle to a common one), the complexes of finite Tor amplitude form a
thick subcategory. Its intersection with the triangulated subcategory
$D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ is again a full triangulated subcategory.
